neighbours.label: locating a place relative to another place: the locating word or place name in 'two blocks from…', 'in downtown X', 'a village outside X'
fire: The hostel is in a quiet street three blocks from the main railway station, next to a bakery and a small park that fills with families at the weekend.
The trade fair is held every October at the convention centre in downtown Milwaukee.
His aunt and uncle run a small farm in the hills outside Kampala.
The new library stands just a block from the old town hall, across the road from the covered market and the bus depot.
They opened their first restaurant in a narrow lane behind the cathedral in downtown Quito.
The clinic occupies the ground floor of an office building two blocks from the river, near the footbridge that leads to the university.
She grew up in a fishing town a few miles south of Bergen.
The film school is housed in a former brewery a short walk from the harbour in Gdansk.
quiet: The hostel is quiet and cheap, with a shared kitchen and a small garden that fills with guests at the weekend.
The trade fair is held every October and attracts thousands of buyers.
His aunt and uncle keep goats and grow a little maize and coffee.
The new library opened last year, with a reading room for children and a large collection of maps.
Milwaukee has agreed a new budget, and Quito plans to do the same next month.
The clinic treats about forty patients a day, most of them students from the university.
She grew up in a family of teachers and learned to read early.
The film school accepts thirty students a year and charges no fees.

notes: Card: no single token; top examples are city names and locatives after in/at/from/outside. Probes: 'two blocks from' 0.46-0.47 (peak ' blocks'), 'in downtown Denver' 0.36, 'a village outside Nairobi' 0.35, 'college in Lisbon' 0.11, city as subject 0.03-0.15.
